title: Closing the Logarithmic Gap in Beck's Circle Discrepancy Bound

problemStatement.formal: c\,\sqrt{r} \le \inf_A f_A(r) \le C\,\sqrt{r \log r}, \quad \text{where } f_A(r) = \sup_C |\#(A \cap C) - \pi r^2|; \text{ is the extremal rate } \Theta(\sqrt{r}) \text{ or } \Theta(\sqrt{r \log r})?
problemStatement.plain: Beck proved the circle discrepancy of any infinite planar point set is at least about sqrt(r), and that a randomized set keeps it near sqrt(r log r). A factor of sqrt(log r) separates these bounds. The open question: is the truth sqrt(r) (log removable) or sqrt(r log r) (log forced)? We formalize the gap and prove the squeeze/dichotomy lemmas framing it.
whyMatters: Flagship open sub-question of an otherwise solved Erdős problem — closing it gives the exact order of circle discrepancy.
The analogous log-gap question drives modern geometric discrepancy theory (boxes, half-planes, spheres).
Formalizing the precise statement and reduction lemmas makes the open problem machine-checkable.

proven: Beck's universal lower bound f_A(r) ≫ √r for all A (beck_lower_bound axiom in erdos-989).
Beck's existence upper bound ∃A, f_A(r) ≪ √(r log r) (beck_upper_bound axiom, beckOptimalSequence witness).
Unboundedness f_A(r) → ∞ for every A (discrepancy_unbounded theorem).
open: Whether inf_A f_A(r) has order √r or √(r log r).
Whether Beck's √(log r) union-bound loss over O(r²) circle centers is intrinsic or an artifact.
Whether any explicit (non-randomized) sequence attains O(√(r log r)).
knownResults.goal: Formalize the open problem precisely: define g(r) = inf_A f_A(r), state Conjectures A (log removable) and B (log forced), prove the squeeze lemma (c√r ≤ g(r) ≤ C√(r log r)) from the existing Beck axioms, and prove the dichotomy lemma that A and B are mutually exclusive since √(log r) → ∞. Resolving the gap itself is out of scope.
